title: Maximize Amount After Two Days of Conversions
summary: Given an initial amount of 1.0 of a specified currency, you are provided with conversion pairs and rates for two days.
statement: Given an initial amount of 1.0 of a specified currency, you are provided with conversion pairs and rates for two days. On day 1, use pairs1 for conversions at rates1, and on day 2, use pairs2 for conversions at rates2. Each target currency can be converted back to its start currency at a rate of 1 divided by the original rate. Perform any number of conversions on each day to maximize the initial amount. Conversion rates are consistent, and there are no contradictions in the rates for either day.
constraints: Each day has 1–10 consistent currency pairs with positive rates and reciprocal reverse conversions.
Start day one with one unit of initial_currency; carry one resulting currency into day two and finish in the initial currency.
Use any number of conversions per day and return the maximum final amount.
hints: Consistent conversion graphs assign one relative value to every currency reachable from the initial currency.
Compute initial-to-currency ratios for each day, then combine day one forward with day two backward.
Traverse both graphs with reciprocal edges; maximize day1[currency]/day2[currency] over common currencies.
Any same-day path has the stored consistent ratio, and every two-day plan is determined by its overnight currency.
editorial: Any same-day path has the stored consistent ratio, and every two-day plan is determined by its overnight currency.

tests.explanation: Six JPY after day one converts through day two at 120 EUR per JPY, yielding 720.
The same rate both days offers no gain, so retain one unit.
